description: Scythian goldsmithing was one of the most distinctive artistic traditions of the ancient Eurasian steppe. Skilled craftsmen produced finely worked gold plaques, belt fittings, jewelry, weapon decorations, and horse-harness ornaments, often using casting, repoussé, engraving, and granulation. Their famous “animal style” featured dynamic stags, felines, birds of prey, horses, and mythical creatures arranged in compact, flowing compositions. Many surviving masterpieces come from richly furnished kurgan burials, where gold objects signaled status, identity, and elite warrior culture.
